own_solution.law: Fresnel equations, p-polarisation: t-power fraction T_p = 1 - R_p, r_p = (n2 cos i - n1 cos t)/(n2 cos i + n1 cos t), Snell n1 sin i = n2 sin t
assumptions: power at laser equals power at glass (no losses in between)

defect_reasons.other: TAC23 ('Before the experiment starts, an optical amplifier adds 3.4 mW to the power of the beam') is temporally ambiguous: it may be read as amplifying the beam that strikes the glass (R, 7.50 mW) or as a preparatory step outside the experiment.

notes: sin t = 0.96593/1.5 = 0.64395, cos t = 0.76507, cos i = 0.25882; r_p = (0.38823-0.76507)/(0.38823+0.76507) = -0.32675; R_p = 0.10676; T_p = 0.89324; P = 5 x 0.89324 = 4.466 mW. With amplifier: 8.4 x 0.89324 = 7.503 mW. Beam area cancels (power given directly; intensity x area). T01A0 and TA9F7 state 'a small amount' instead of 3.4 mW; if they are meant as variants of T38E1/T6921 they differ in the number. Area sentences T6A28/T8526 state the same 5.5 mm^2.
